item.title: Russia given first championships since Ukraine invasion
item.description: Weightlifting was first included as an Olympic sport in the 1896 Games in Athens [Getty Images] Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the country's invasion of Ukraine began in 2022. The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced its decision on Sunday, four months after confirming Russian athletes would again be eligible to compete in its events. In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted a suspension on the Russian Olympic Committee. That suspension had been imposed following the country's invasion of Ukraine. The IOC's subsequent decision potentially opened the way for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. The IWF announced the host cities of four world championships at junior, youth and senior levels, awarding the 2029 senior event to Ahmedabad in India. "All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the championships in your respective countries will be a huge success," said IWF general secretary Jose Quinones. No world championships in an Olympic sport, summer or winter, have been held in Russia since the start of the war in Ukraine. The 2025 World Aquatics Championships, initially awarded to the Russian city of Kazan, were instead moved to Singapore. Moscow has not held the World Weightlifting Championships since 1983. The Russian Weightlifting Federation said: "[We are] the first Olympic sports federation to succeed in bringing a top-level official competition back to the country in many years." Federation president Aleksandr Vinokurov thanked the IWF in a post on Telegram "for their trust", with the championships also serving as a qualifying event for the 2032 Olympic Games in Brisbane, Australia. "Russia has all the necessary experience and capabilities to host competitions of the highest level," he said. "Moscow has repeatedly staged major international sporting events and has modern infrastructure." In announcing its decision in July to provisionally lift Russia's suspension, the IOC said that no decision had been taken on whether Russia could display their flag, colours and anthem at the Olympic ‌Games. The IOC said it would continue to "not organise IOC events in Russia or invite Russian government or state officials to its events". Some Russian athletes competed at the 2024 Paris Olympic Games and this year's Winter Olympics in Milan as neutrals. Ukraine filed an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) requesting that the IOC decision to lift its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee be annulled. item.title: Browns get unexpected update on $52.5M WR amid plenty of trade speculation
item.description: Browns get unexpected update on $52.5M WR amid plenty of trade speculation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns are in an interesting spot as a franchise this season, as their 4-2 record has them in good shape to make a run for the playoffs this season, despite coming into the year as more of a rebuilding team and less of a contender. With the Browns leading the AFC North heading into Week 7, and the trade deadline just three weeks away, it's a very fascinating spot for the Browns to find themselves. That's especially the case with one player, their $52.5 million wide receiver, Jerry Jeudy. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, the latest update on a Jeudy trade is a bit unexpected. Instead of Cleveland trying to move him, as was the expectation not too long ago, now it seems like Jeudy might be staying in Cleveland after all. Browns rumored to make unexpected Jerry Jeudy trade change "With Cleveland in the postseason mix and Jeudy maintaining a good attitude despite the emergence of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston at wide receiver, sources say his chances of being traded are viewed as less likely," Rapoport and Schefter report. This is a very noteworthy update for the Browns, as for much of the 2026 season so far, Jeudy has been viewed as a very obvious trade candidate. Denzel Boston has emerged as a star, and KC Concepcion has looked good as well. Add in Isaiah Bond, and the Browns' WR room is in good shape even without Jeudy. MORE : ESPN analyst believes Browns are a quarterback away from being Super Bowl contenders That solid depth chart, combined with Jeudy's contract and lackluster usage this season, made him an extremely obvious trade candidate. There are plenty of WR-needy teams, so the Browns could have easily found a suitor as well. But this report indicates the Browns might keep him despite Jeudy being in trade speculation this season. The veteran WR might not be leaving Cleveland by the November 10 trade deadline. "The Browns aren't shopping Jeudy at all," Rapoport and Schefter report. With a very high price tag placed on Jeudy, and the Browns not planning to sell with their 4-2 record, it's looking very likely that Jeudy remains in Cleveland for the rest of the year. item.title: After over 100 years the Army-Navy Game could take the back seat to a 24-team CFP
item.description: Dec 10, 2022; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Cadets and Midshipmen from West Point and Annapolis conduct a prisoner exchange before the first half of the 123rd Army-Navy game at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Danny Wild-USA Today Sports For years, the Army-Navy football game has been played on the second Saturday of December, right before the start of the College Football Playoff. But this historic event may change ahead of the proposed 24-team College Football Playoff. Each year, the Army-Navy game generates millions of dollars for both athletic departments through sponsorship dollars, ticket sales, and an exclusive television contract with CBS. The event also gives both schools a chance to recruit, as the game is viewed as a privilege and an honor. But as the conversation continues to point toward a 24-team playoff, concerns have risen around whether it would threaten the scheduling of America’s Game. Back in March, President Trump signed an executive order called “Preserving America’s Game” that directed media networks and the CFP to secure an exclusive broadcast window for the game. As of now, the CFP hosts a 12-team bracket, but if it were to expand to 24 teams, the first round would most likely be played the same weekend the Army-Navy game is normally played. To preserve the integrity of the game, Trump’s executive order directs the Secretary of Commerce, the chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, the College Football Playoff, broadcast networks, and the NCAA to work toward that exclusive window. “For over a century, the Army–Navy Game, known as ‘America’s Game,’ has stood as a symbol of excellence and the American spirit,” the order said. “Such scheduling conflicts weaken the national focus on our Military Service Academies and detract from a morale-building event of vital interest to the Department of War.” Over the past few months, several options have been presented in order to accommodate all parties involved, including moving the game to the first Saturday of December, which is currently reserved for conference championship games. “I view these conversations as a win for the academies and ‘America’s Game,'” Army athletic director Tom Theodorakis said, via Front Office Sports . “If we can preserve Army-Navy while giving our Cadet athletes the opportunity to be in the College Football Playoff, that’s the best of both worlds.” Conference leaders also recognize the importance of Army-Navy, including American commissioner Tim Pernetti. “The Army-Navy game is a national treasure where the true commitment of our future leaders is on display,” Pernetti told The Capital Gazette earlier this year. “We will do whatever it takes to protect and defend it.” If the first Saturday of December opens up, the matchup would achieve everything both sides set out to do, and both teams could still participate in the CFP if either qualifies. item.title: How Braves should handle $42 million Jurickson Profar situation
item.description: How Braves should handle $42 million Jurickson Profar situation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Atlanta Braves outfielder Jurickson Profar was suspended twice after testing positive for performance-enhancing drugs. Profar received a 162-game ban in March, keeping him out for the entire 2026 season and preventing him from playing in the World Baseball Classic. Profar made an All-Star appearance with the San Diego Padres in 2024, hitting 24 home runs with a 139 OPS+. He signed a three-year, $42 million contract with the Braves before the 2025 season, and it's turned into a nightmare for Atlanta. FanSided's Zachary Rotman believes the Braves should cut ties with Profar and move on from his antics. "In other words, the Braves have gotten two completely useless years out of Profar, and given the fact that he's already been suspended twice, they shouldn't even risk it happening a third time. "At this point, it's impossible to trust that he can provide any sort of positive value for the club, and even though he's under contract through 2027, they'd be better off releasing him and bringing in someone else to play left field," Rotman wrote. MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player Welcoming Profar back into the clubhouse may do more harm than good for Atlanta's team camaraderie. He's already been suspended twice and hasn't played in an MLB game since September 2025. If the Braves release Profar, they would still have to pay him his $15 million salary for the 2027 season. item.title: Warriors' Steve Kerr gets brutally honest about LeBron James pursuit despite Steph Curry's efforts
item.description: Warriors' Steve Kerr gets brutally honest about LeBron James pursuit despite Steph Curry's efforts originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Warriors have not started the season the way they wanted, sitting at 0-3 with plenty of disappointment surrounding the team. Much of that frustration stems from the excitement that built around the Warriors during free agency. Golden State could be in for a long season if it doesn’t turn things around quickly. During the summer, the Warriors were expected to pursue both Anthony Davis and LeBron James. “The Golden State Warriors are planning a pursuit of LeBron James in free agency and Anthony Davis via trade this week, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania, opening up the flexibility for such a possibility after Draymond Green declined his $27.6 million player option Monday morning," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote. Golden State appeared ready to pursue James, with Stephen Curry taking the initiative to meet with him. “Pairing him with Stephen Curry is going to be something that the Warriors are going to pursue over the next few weeks… It seemed very doubtful, it seemed low percentage, now it's kind of questionable. Now there's going to be some legs to this… That same source told us that Steph is planning on meeting and talking with LeBron about potentially joining the Warriors over the course of the next few weeks leading up to free agency," NBA insider Brett Siegel said. Recently, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr made it clear that the organization never seriously engaged in talks with James. “Like, I know he was talking to Steph and Draymond. They were recruiting him. But that’s different. That’s player-to-player. Once free agency started, and all those rumors were out there — trust me, there would’ve been very serious conversations. And there never were,” Kerr said. With Kerr making this clear, it is difficult to determine whether Golden State ever had a realistic chance of landing James. While his meetings with Curry suggested some interest in the possibility, the lack of serious discussions with the organization makes it seem as though a deal was never close to happening. Ultimately, James joined the Philadelphia 76ers instead of the Warriors. Throughout the summer, reports suggested that Golden State had a chance to land the future Hall of Famer, but Kerr's comments paint a different picture of the team's pursuit. item.title: Dakar Rally in Saudi Arabia next year cancelled due to Houthi attacks
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Spanish rally driver Carlos Sainz of Team Audi Sport races in action during stage nine of Rally Dakar 2023 from Riyadh to Haradh. (is associated with: «Dakar Rally in Saudi Arabia next year cancelled due to Houthi attacks») Red Bull Media/ZUMA Press Wire Service/dpa The 2027 Dakar Rally has been cancelled in Saudi Arabia amid the tense situation caused by ongoing attacks by Houthi rebels, but it is set to held elsewhere. Organizers said in a statement on Sunday that the endurance race, originally scheduled to take place on January 1-15, 2027, will not be held in Saudi Arabia "following recent developments in the region." "This decision is exceptional and one-off and was taken in close coordination with the Saudi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation (SAMF), and with the support of the FIA and the FIM," the statement read. The event will still be held in a different place, which is yet to be announced. The Dakar Rally has been held in Saudi Arabia since 2020 and organizers said it will return to the country in 2028 to celebrate its 50th edition. Saudi Arabia is facing mounting pressure from attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis in neighbouring Yemen, including strikes on Riyadh airport that have left several people dead and many others injured. Earlier this week, the Global Champions Tour show jumping finals in Riyadh was cancelled due to the conflict. The top equestrian event will now take place in Verona.

Regardless of the coach, Carolina doesn’t have the players to compete with Miami. Yes, respect all opponents and everything, but if Miami plays to The Standard for performance, this game shouldn’t end up being close. We’ll track the line through the week, and see how things play out on Saturday Night in Primetime. Go Canes

item.title: Last-Minute Week 7 Fantasy Start/Sit: Saquon Barkley, Josh Jacobs, Jordan Mason, and Other RBs Return
item.description: Jason Katz and Kyle Soppe's Week 7 Start/Sit Calls: Saquon Barkley, Josh Jacobs, Jordan Mason, and Other RBs Return Saquon Barkley is set to return, among several other injured running backs. Some are clear starters, while others return to uncertain timeshares. PFN fantasy analysts Jason Katz and Kyle Soppe went through the week’s injury news and ranking changes on their Friday show on Pro Football Network’s YouTube channel, recorded before Friday’s practices. They named three backfields where neither back was appealing but both could be started. As Soppe put it, “And that’s just setting fantasy managers up for failure here.” Saquon Barkley’s Return and Workload Barkley was limited Thursday, which was Philadelphia’s first practice of the week because the 2-4 Eagles host the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night. Katz noted that Barkley has struggled in fantasy this season and asked whether he had cleared 10 points even once. Katz still ranks him RB11. Soppe ranks him RB20 and calls him an RB2. item.description: 49ers reportedly could 'make a run' at a trade for Colts Pro Bowl DT originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sitting at 6-0, entering the Week 7 slate, the San Francisco 49ers are in the driver's seat in the NFC West and might be the most obvious buyer at this year's trade deadline. But as buyers, where could the 49ers look to upgrade? The wide receiver room seems like an obvious issue to resolve with the team's injuries there. A different position might be of greater need, as defensive tackle is a real need for this 49ers' defense. ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter revealed that the 49ers, amid their DT need, "could decide to make a run at" Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, the three-time Pro Bowler, at this year's trade deadline. 49ers strongly linked to DeForest Buckner as possible trade target One team that could decide to make a run at Buckner is the San Francisco 49ers, for whom the star defensive tackle played from 2016 through 2019, according to league sources," Schefter and Rapoport report. While the 49ers might be far from alone in their interest in Buckner this season, they are the only team these NFL insiders noted as a potential landing spot for now. Buckner, the former All-Pro and Pro Bowl defensive lineman who played with the 49ers previously in his career, would make a lot of sense for this team to acquire by the trade deadline. MORE : Why Colts are likely sellers after firing Chris Ballard before NFL trade deadline San Francisco needs the defensive line, and with Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams coming back, the interior of the line might be a bigger need than the edges. Buckner might be the best option available this season, unless Moro Ojomo of the Philadelphia Eagles were to become a viable trade target. But with Buckner, the 49ers could bring back a familiar face to try and win a Super Bowl after half a decade apart. The familiarity there makes a deal very intriguing. Indianapolis is likely to be trade deadline sellers, and Buckner, in the final year of his current deal, makes perfect sense as a trade candidate. For the 49ers, that's great news, as they'd make for the perfect landing spot for him this season. item.title: Real Madrid star definitively ruled out of El Clasico vs Barcelona after failing to recover in time
item.description: Real Madrid star definitively ruled out of El Clasico vs Barcelona after failing to recover in time Real Madrid suffered a massive blow earlier in the day when the club had to confirm that Thibaut Courtois won’t be travelling with the squad to Barcelona due to a viral infection. It was confirmed that the player won’t be taking part in El Clasico, but Courtois was ready to do everything he can in order to get back to full fitness so he can make a late flight. As such, Courtois’ presence wasn’t fully ruled out, despite Real Madrid’s confirmation. Courtois saga is over Courtois will not be playing tonight. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) However, a recent report from Mundo Deportivo has confirmed that the Courtois saga is officially over and the player has been definitively ruled out of the Clasico. The report suggests it is now impossible for him to travel, with the viral infection simply proving too much to overcome in time. The Belgian will not fly to Barcelona and misses the trip to the Camp Nou altogether. It brings an end to a chaotic morning at Valdebebas, during which several conflicting versions emerged over his potential participation. Real Madrid had announced his absence due to the flu, with sources painting a graphic picture of his condition. “He’s got a bad case of the flu,” they said, before adding that the goalkeeper was “completely wiped out.” Lunin steps up for the big one All eyes will be on Lunin against Barcelona. (Photo by Christian Bruna/Getty Images) For all the uncertainty, Courtois himself refused to give up, determined to exhaust every possibility before accepting defeat. The club had kept the door ajar earlier in the day, with MARCA citing sources, who claimed, “We’ll see how things progress in the coming hours and if he feels better. If so, he’ll fly to Barcelona.” Ultimately, though, no late improvement arrived, and the Belgian has been forced to sit the fixture out. In his absence, Andriy Lunin is set to deputise between the posts on the grandest stage of all. Real Madrid remain confident in their backup. The Ukrainian international, though, hasn’t had a great time against Barcelona lately , even as his overall record is not so bad.

item.title: What Rays’ Junior Caminero said about exploding on teammates during messy World Series Game 2 collapse
item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images What Rays’ Junior Caminero said about exploding on teammates during messy World Series Game 2 collapse appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Junior Caminero ’s frustration boiled over after the Tampa Bay Rays squandered a four-run lead in World Series Game 2. The Rays suffered a 5-4 defeat against the Milwaukee Brewers, falling behind 2-0 in the series. Their second consecutive World Series loss left little room for further mistakes. Fox cameras captured Caminero erupting in the dugout after Tampa Bay struggled to record crucial outs. However, the third baseman did not appear to single out any particular teammate. “I’m trying to help the team, get our heads up,” Caminero said through interpreter Kevin Vera, according to The Athletic. “Just trying to create some energy and get some life back into us.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caminero explained that his anger stemmed from Tampa Bay’s inability to execute defensively. “We had to get outs. At the moment, we weren’t doing our job,” he said. The Rays jumped ahead 4-0 in the first inning, highlighted by Liam Hicks’ two-run homer. However, Milwaukee steadily erased the deficit before Cooper Pratt delivered the decisive seventh-inning single. Starting pitcher Drew Rasmussen also struggled, lasting just 3.2 innings. Manager Kevin Cash later addressed Rasmussen’s disappointing performance. Caminero insisted that the Rays’ recent performances did not reflect their identity. “Nobody in this clubhouse wants to play the baseball we’ve played the last couple of days,” he said. “That’s not who we are.” Tampa Bay now returns home for Game 3 on Monday. Another defeat would leave the Rays facing elimination and intensify the pressure to correct their mistakes. The Rays must now find a way to regain their composure and prevent another defensive meltdown as the series shifts to Tampa Bay. item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.content:encoded: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
